readme:
# Theseus A grounded semantic graph whose structure comes from ontology and whose meaning comes from a consumer-owned Topology. > Current implementation: v0.2.0 local prototype > Release status: built and locally red-teamed, not deployed, not production > grade, and not commercial quality Created by Stanley Fich as research informing JadeIQ. JadeIQ stewards AEGIS and the Theseus reference implementation. > **Historical inquiry disclaimer:** "the Nazis won World War II" is the > prototype's adversarial research prompt, not an endorsed conclusion. Theseus, > Stanley Fich, and JadeIQ do not promote or endorse that statement. The case > was chosen to force support, rejection, qualification, and provenance to do > serious work against a historically consequential claim. ## Table of contents - [About the project](#about-the-project) - [AEGIS and project identity](#aegis-and-project-identity) - [The hypothesis](#the-hypothesis) - [Implications](#implications) - [Potential applications](#potential-applications) - [Scope](#scope) - [The model](#the-model) - [Definition plane](#definition-plane) - [Data and provenance plane](#data-and-provenance-plane) - [Topology plane](#topology-plane) - [Consumer plane](#consumer-plane) - [Prototype scenario](#prototype-scenario) - [Implemented proof](#implemented-proof) - [Packages](#packages) - [Technology](#technology) - [Run it](#run-it) - [Verification and provenance](#verification-and-provenance) - [Iterations and learnings](#iterations-and-learnings) - [Roadmap](#roadmap) - [What v0.2.0 demonstrates](#what-v020-demonstrates) - [Possible improvements](#possible-improvements) - [License and contributing](#license-and-contributing) - [Acknowledgements](#acknowledgements) ## About the project Most graph systems can store vertices and edges without deciding what a useful arrangement means. Record schemas can validate each item while leaving endpoint meaning, evidence rules, and graph-wide constraints in UI switches, prose, or a separate reasoner. Theseus gives those responsibilities explicit owners: - `@theseus/ontology` owns stable identities, executable Definitions, neutral graph records, evidence provenance, append-only history, settlement, and the closed Topology language. - A consumer owns its Lexicon and concrete Topology. The first consumer is `@theseus/thesis`. - Consumer commands are the current UI and reducer write boundary and the intended boundary for future agent and transport clients. - Consumer projections turn qualified ontology state into application concepts that a UI can render. The thesis workbench starts with an Utterance: ```text "the nazis won wwII" ``` The phrase is not accepted as a conclusion. The fixture separates four possible readings, grounds researched assertions in captured Sources and exact Evidence, then records how each assertion supports, rejects, qualifies, or contextualizes one reading. The UI keeps the source record and the consumer's inference visibly separate. The complete implementation contract is in [ARCHITECTURE.md](ARCHITECTURE.md). ## AEGIS and project identity The project uses three names for three different responsibilities: - **AEGIS** is the Astro Epistemic Graph Interpretation Specification, the proposed portable contract for the model and its guarantees. - **Theseus** is the TypeScript reference implementation and proving ground for AEGIS. - **JadeIQ** stewards the research and is its production expression. The public prototype does not claim that those production systems are implemented here. [AEGIS: A topology of trust for human-machine knowledge work](aegis.md) is the working abstract and paper plan. It defines the claim the paper must earn, the guarantee a normative specification should make, candidate code samples, and the questions that remain open. It is not yet a normative specification. ## The hypothesis Theseus asks whether one reusable ontology can support several applications without absorbing their local meanings. > Can ontology provide durable graph mechanics while an application supplies a > local vocabulary and an executable account of what connected resources mean? V0.2.0 tests four claims: 1. Definitions can provide stable structural vocabulary without encoding application endpoint semantics. 2. Every property assertion can enter the graph with complete Evidence-to-Source provenance and retain append-only correction history. 3. A closed Topology language can interpret and constrain graph arrangements without persisted roles or application callbacks in ontology. 4. Consumers can expose their own commands and projections over the same ontology package. This is not an RDF or OWL implementation. Theseus does not provide open-world entailment or a global reasoner. It evaluates one bounded graph snapshot under one exact consumer-owned Topology revision and returns inspectable bindings or named violations. ## Implications The longer argument is in [Implications of Theseus v0.2.0](implications.readme.md). Its working claims are: - bounded operations and reproducible interpretation can support trust without asking a reviewer to accept a model's answer on confidence alone; - ontology can enforce identity, structure, provenance, and lifecycle while a consumer-owned Topology supplies local meaning; - the same command types are designed for future human and agent clients, but v0.2.0 has no live agent, principal authentication, or review policy; - append-only correction preserves disagreement inside retained state, but unanchored digests cannot prevent wholesale history replacement; - the current map, Evidence ledger, and Topology report share one qualified research state, while document, chart, and timeline generation remains prospective; and - the standards comparison classifies Theseus as a qualified synthesis whose direct comparator is SHACL, not RDF or OWL in isolation. Those claims are implications of a local prototype, not production findings. The completed standards comparison narrows their novelty and trust language. The remaining engineering work includes stronger source custody, remote conformance, collaboration, a complete second consumer, and larger graph evaluation. ## Potential applications Theseus v0.2.0 is one local thesis workbench, not a suite of shipped vertical products. The reusable idea applies where people and future agent clients build contestable conclusions from exact evidence under a shared executable contract. The [full applications adjudication](implications.readme.md#potential-applications) covers 30 distinct product contracts. This table keeps the five decision questions visible at a more useful README scale. | Application family | One-line pitch | Why it matters | Theseus distinction | Systems in the vicinity | Why the agentic era changes the job | | ----------------------------- | ------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------ | ------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------ | ------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- | ------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- | -------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- | | Research and argument | Build reviewable research, legal matters, investigations, policy analysis, and scientific syntheses from exact evidence. | Source fact, interpretation, conflict, and conclusion must remain distinguishable. | Atomic Claim-to-Evidence-to-Source admission, bearing relations, a pinned Topology, and explicit correction history. | [Harvey](https://www.harvey.ai/platform), [Legora](https://legora.com/product/legal-research), [Zotero](https://www.zotero.org/support/quick_start_guide), and [OCCRP Aleph](https://docs.aleph.occrp.org/about/) serve neighboring jobs. | Agents can search and extract at scale; acceptance still needs a bounded, inspectable path. | | Organizational decisions | Connect customer evidence, roles, skills, talent, compensation, strategy, and decisions. | Inferred signals should not silently become facts about people or priorities. | Consumer-owned Lexicons and Topologies, typed values, explicit Origins, and one closed command language. | [Dovetail](https://dovetail.com/solutions/product-research/), [O*NET](https://www.onetcenter.org/content.html), and [LinkedIn Talent Insights](https://www.linkedin.com/products/linkedin-talent-insights/) hold adjacent data and workflows. | Cheap inference increases the need for owned definitions, reasons, review, correction, and appeal. | | Diligence and assurance | Link obligations, controls, deal disclosures, suppliers, assets, assumptions, tests, and findings. | A reviewer needs the exact source and rule version behind a decision. | Immutable releases, grounded Claims, supersession history, and candidate conformance before in-memory settlement. | [Workiva](https://www.workiva.com/solutions/sec-reporting/), [Datasite](https://www.datasite.com/en/products/diligence), and [ARGUS Enterprise](https://www.altusgroup.com/solutions/argus-enterprise/) are likely integration neighbors. | Agents can assemble a file quickly; accountable professionals still need a reproducible basis. | | Structured creation | Move from mind maps and research through writing, storyboards, content strategy, and campaign approval. | Ideas, factual claims, canon, production state, and publication authority require different treatment. | Drafts can remain outside accepted state, Topology can define valid structure, and several projections can share one qualified graph. | [Miro](https://help.miro.com/hc/en-us/articles/360017730753-Mind-map), [Scrivener](https://www.literatureandlatte.com/scrivener/overview), and [Storyboard Pro](https://www.toonboom.com/products/Storyboard-Pro) remain the production tools nearby. | Generation is abundant; controlled acceptance and source lineage are scarce. | | Public and regulated evidence | Prepare environmental reviews, public cases, clinical evidence, safety assessments, and drug-safety work. | Errors can affect rights, health, safety, and public decisions. | Exact evidence, explicit uncertainty, pinned rules, closed commands, and named approval can form a review contract. | [EPA NEPA](https://www.epa.gov/nepa), [Covidence](https://get.covidence.org/systematic-review-software), [FDA AEMS](https://www.fda.gov/drugs/fdas-adverse-event-reporting-system-faers/fda-adverse-event-reporting-system-faers-public-dashboard), and the [NTSB process](https://www.ntsb.gov/investigations/process/Pages/default.aspx/1000) define mature neighboring work. | Agent assistance is useful only when authority, reasons, review, and correction remain explicit. | | Knowledge and engineering | Map requirements, verification, archival objects, interpretations, curricula, and standards across versions. | Meaning and traceability must survive tool and schema changes. | Stable Definition families, immutable revisions, consumer-owned meaning, Topology evaluation, and explicit lifecycle. | [ReqIF](https://www.omg.org/reqif/), [CIDOC CRM](https://cidoc-crm.org/), and [CASE](https://www.1edtech.org/standards/case) are interoperability neighbors. | Agents can reconcile large knowledge sets, but semantic changes still need governed ownership. | The 30 assessed applications are: 1. general evidence-led research; 2. product discovery and strategy; 3. legal matter research, chronology, evidence, and argument; 4. compliance and internal audit evidence; 5. investigative journalism and OSINT; 6. public policy and regulatory impact analysis; 7. M&A and commercial diligence; 8. procurement and supply-chain diligence; 9. real-estate diligence, underwriting, valuation, and improvement scenarios; 10. investment research and underwriting; 11. scientific literature and reproducibility mapping; 12. workforce planning, role architecture, and skills intelligence; 13. recruiting, success profiles, and competitive talent analysis; 14. compensation architecture and pay-equity analysis; 15. mind mapping; 16. long-form writing; 17. storyboarding and narrative production; 18. content strategy; 19. marketing campaign reasoning; 20. education curriculum and mastery evidence; 21. standards and requirements engineering; 22. environmental review and permitting; 23. cultural heritage and archival interpretation; 24. public-sector benefits, licensing, and casework; 25. cyber incident and threat analysis; 26. human-rights investigation and accountability; 27. clinical evidence review and guideline support; 28. pharmacovigilance and drug-safety signal assessment; 29. insurance underwriting and claims evidence; and 30. safety incident and root-cause investigation. These are application hypotheses, not roadmap promises. Production use needs durable state, principal identity and authorization, collaboration, rich evidence custody, Topology authoring and governance, external integrations, and domain validation. Provenance makes a conclusion inspectable. It does not make the conclusion true. ## Scope V0.2.0 implements two connected pieces. ### Reusable ontology `@theseus/ontology` provides scoped Definition registries, concrete graph resources, grounded Claims, provenance, pure planning, atomic in-memory settlement, supersession, strict hydration, and generic Topology evaluation. It imports no thesis, React, YAML, transport, or persistence code. ### Thesis consumer and local UI `@theseus/thesis` establishes its own SubjectDefs, RelDefs, PropertyDefs, Lexicon release, and Topology through public ontology behavior. Its commands accept thesis keys rather than ontology IDs. The UI gets thesis-specific labels and endpoint meaning from that projection. Its Evidence inspector and Topology report also read trusted ontology authority directly. The browser application is local only. TanStack Router owns navigation, Lexical owns authored prose, React Flow owns graph interaction, and Immer owns finite UI transitions. A strict adapter hydrates the checked-in YAML once at the route boundary. There is no database, server, deployment, or live model call. ## The model ### Definition plane Definition families separate stable, scoped keys from immutable executable revisions. Releases and graph bindings pin exact IDs and content digests. ```mermaid flowchart TB Scope["Contract Scope"] --> Lexicon["Consumer Lexicon"] Lexicon --> SFamily["SubjectDef Family
stable scoped key"] Lexicon --> RFamily["RelDef Family
stable scoped key"] Lexicon --> PFamily["PropertyDef Family
stable scoped key"] SFamily --> SDef["SubjectDef Revision"] RFamily --> RDef["RelDef Revision"] PFamily --> PDef["PropertyDef Revision"] SDef -->|"permits property family"| PFamily RDef -->|"permits property family"| PFamily Release["Lexicon Release
exact Definition IDs + digest"] --> SDef Release --> RDef Release --> PDef Binding["Graph Contract Binding
exact releases + Topology closure"] --> Release ``` - `SubjectDef` defines one kind of Subject and the PropertyDef families it may carry. - `RelDef` defines directed or undirected binary incidence and the PropertyDef families it may carry. - `PropertyDef` defines one value domain in the bounded `theseus.closed-json-schema/v1` language. - A `LexiconRelease` selects exact Definition revisions. - A `GraphContractBinding` authorizes exact release and Topology bytes for new graph plans. RelDef has no endpoint roles, type selectors, application cardinalities, labels, usage prose, callbacks, or lifecycle switches. Thesis expresses those meanings through Topology. ### Data and provenance plane Subjects and Rels pin exact Definitions. An ontology Claim is one typed value about one Subject or Rel. Every Claim settles with at least one complete attachment chain. ```mermaid flowchart LR SDef["SubjectDef"] -->|"structures"| Subject["Subject"] RDef["RelDef"] -->|"structures"| Rel["Rel"] PDef["PropertyDef"] -->|"validates"| Claim["Ontology Claim"] Rel -->|"source or member"| Left["Graph Resource"] Rel -->|"target or member"| Right["Graph Resource"] Claim -->|"owner"| Subject Claim -->|"owner"| Rel Attachment["EvidenceAttachment"] --> Claim Attachment --> Evidence["Evidence
exact UTF-16 span"] Evidence --> Source["Source
captured text + digest"] Origin["Origin"] -.->|"records creation"| Subject Origin -.->|"records creation"| Rel Origin -.->|"records creation"| Claim Origin -.->|"records creation"| Evidence Origin -.->|"records creation"| Source Newer["New Claim or Rel"] -->|"system supersedes"| Older["Historical Claim or Rel"] ``` There is no persisted `PropertyValue` and no detached Evidence workflow. One grounded-Claim plan contains the Claim, fresh EvidenceAttachments, and either new or existing Evidence and Source references. Settlement commits every new record in that plan or none of them. Claims and ordinary Rels never change in place. A correction creates a grounded successor and a system-owned `supersedes` Rel. Current-head projection follows that lifecycle relation, never Origin time or array order. Concurrent heads remain visible until a consumer records another successor. ### Topology plane Definitions govern one record at a time. Topology governs meaningful arrangements. ```mermaid flowchart LR Release["Pinned Lexicon Release"] --> Topology["Consumer Topology Revision"] Binding["Graph Contract Binding"] --> Topology Snapshot["Trusted Graph Snapshot"] --> Evaluate["Ontology Evaluator"] Candidate["Authenticated AppendPlan"] --> Evaluate Topology --> Evaluate Evaluate --> Matches["Canonical Bindings"] Evaluate --> Violations["Named Violations"] Matches --> Projection["Consumer Projection"] Matches --> Gate["Settlement Gate"] Violations --> Guidance["User or Agent Guidance"] Violations --> Refusal["No Settlement"] ``` Ontology owns `theseus.topology/v1`, its parser, static checks, deterministic evaluator, indexes, quotas, and result types. Thesis owns the concrete `argument-core` family and revision. Rules bind exact Subjects, Rels, Claims, Sources, Evidence, attachments, current heads, and bounded paths. They can require type, direction, existence, absence, value, cardinality, distinctness, and containment. Variables such as `$claim` and `$target` exist only during evaluation. They are not persisted roles. A valid graph can fail one selected interpretation. The evaluator reports that as `conforms: false` with stable violations. Malformed ontology, malformed Topology, unauthenticated candidate plans, and exhausted work quotas return separate structured problems. ### Consumer plane Each application establishes its contract once, exposes bounded commands, and projects only qualified state. ```mermaid flowchart TB subgraph Consumer["Consumer Package"] Lexicon["Local Lexicon"] Topologies["Pinned Topology Revisions"] Commands["Consumer Commands"] Projection["Domain Projection"] end User["User"] --> Commands Agent["Agent"] --> Commands Commands --> Planner["Ontology Planner"] Lexicon --> Planner Planner --> Evaluate["Candidate Evaluation"] Topologies --> Evaluate Evaluate -->|"conforms"| Settle["Atomic Settlement"] Evaluate -->|"violations"| Commands Settle --> State["Trusted Ontology State"] State --> Projection Topologies --> Projection Projection --> Research["Research Workbench
implemented"] Projection --> MindMap["Mind Map
possible consumer"] Projection --> Storyboard["Storyboard
boundary proof"] ``` The implemented consumer pattern is: 1. Establish the Lexicon, exact release, and Topology through ontology. 2. Store the resulting exact IDs and digests in a consumer manifest. 3. Decode untrusted input through a closed command union, then resolve consumer keys rather than accepting ontology IDs. 4. Plan through ontology, authenticate and evaluate the candidate, then settle the same plan only if it conforms. 5. Project trusted graph state and exact Topology bindings into application concepts. The repository includes a narrow second-consumer storyboard boundary test. It creates a separate Lexicon, Definitions, Topology, graph binding, and two Scene Subjects, then plans a candidate `precedes` Rel and evaluates it as conforming. The test does not settle that Rel or implement a storyboard package, projection, or UI. It adds no storyboard branches to ontology. ## Prototype scenario The canonical fixture treats the Utterance seriously enough to stress the model. It separates these readings: | Reading | Meaning | Research assertions | | ------------------------- | -------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- | ------------------: | | Literal military victory | Nazi Germany achieved the prevailing military and sovereign outcome | 4 | | Coordinated broader plan | The war concealed a centrally coordinated postwar Nazi plan | 6 | | Postwar persistence | Some personnel, expertise, institutions, networks, or ideology survived or were reused | 14 | | Irreversible consequences | Nazi rule produced catastrophic outcomes before its defeat | 2 | The 26 researched assertions use 12 support, 7 reject, 1 context, and 6 qualify bearings. None supports the coordinated-plan reading. The fixture can therefore show military defeat, postwar persistence, and irreversible harm at the same time without laundering one meaning into another. The checked-in state contains: | Record | Count | | ----------------------------- | ----: | | Thesis interpretations | 4 | | Researched assertion Subjects | 26 | | Subjects | 90 | | Rels | 103 | | Ontology property Claims | 193 | | Sources | 172 | | Evidence records | 172 | | EvidenceAttachments | 193 | Twenty-one research assertions also have an honest neutral domain arrangement and a `formalizes` Rel from the natural-language Thesis Claim. Five remain grounded Thesis Claim Subjects with consumer bearings because the current thesis Lexicon has no precise neutral edge for the fact. The fixture does not substitute a nearby relation to make the graph look complete. The browser has four route-selectable views: - Map projects thesis meaning into React Flow nodes and directed, selectable edges. - Argument groups every assertion under the four readings and exposes each bearing. - Evidence traverses all 193 Claim-to-attachment-to-Evidence-to-Source chains. - Topology shows the exact revision, graph binding, SHA-256 digest, rules, matches, and conformance result. The compose dialog authors Claim text and Source text through Lexical, chooses a bearing and target, and selects an exact half-open Evidence span. A local Immer transaction validates the current runtime, recomputes authoritative projection data, executes thesis commands, and publishes the new workspace only after every step succeeds. A successful interaction adds one Thesis Claim Subject, one bearing Rel, two grounded ontology Claims, one Source, one Evidence record, and two EvidenceAttachments. The fixture and its simulated research-agent work live in [`prototype.state.yaml`](prototype.state.yaml). It is the tracked public record of the accepted Sources, Evidence spans, graph facts, and exact authority. ## Implemented proof V0.2.0 meets the experiment's implementation gates: - [x] `@theseus/ontology` stands alone and contains no thesis vocabulary. - [x] Thesis establishes 39 local Definition families, its exact release, one Topology family, and one 26-rule Topology revision through ontology. With the system `supersedes` family, the authority contains 40 families. - [x] Every committed Claim has one or more complete Evidence chains. - [x] Claim and Rel correction is append only through system supersession. - [x] Candidate evaluation authenticates the same plan bytes later settlement receives. - [x] Definition, Topology, and graph authority is behavior-earned, deeply frozen, and rejected after plain object copying. - [x] Strict cold-start hydration replays stored authority and refuses a one-sided Definition or Topology forgery. - [x] The canonical prototype corpus passes the fixed Topology work budget. - [x] A storyboard boundary test plans and evaluates another consumer contract without ontology changes. - [x] The UI gets thesis meaning from thesis projections and sends edits through thesis commands. Trusted Evidence and Topology views read ontology authority directly. - [x] The full test suite, typecheck, lint, and production build pass. - [x] Definition, Topology, corpus, and UI work received adversarial review. Passing these gates is not permission to deploy. The repository remains an unreleased local experiment for human review. ## Packages ### `@theseus/ontology` The ordinary package boundary exports: - registry creation and Definition transitions; - closed JSON validation; - graph creation, planning, candidate authentication, settlement, lifecycle, and read helpers; and - Topology registration, graph-binding authority, and evaluation. Strict restoration from untrusted storage is deliberately separate at `@theseus/ontology/adapter`. Ordinary callers cannot turn object literals or JSON round trips into executable authority. ### `@theseus/thesis` Thesis owns: - four PropertyDef keys, 13 SubjectDef keys, and 22 RelDef keys; - the source-controlled manifest and presentation metadata; - the `argument-core` Topology and its 26 rules; - bounded commands for Subjects, Rels, grounded Claims, and corrections; - strict runtime decoding with stable input refusals for JavaScript and future transport callers; - runtime-manifest validation; and - projections for resources, relations, property Claims, provenance, qualification, and lifecycle history. ### `@theseus/ui` The workspace root assembles: - TanStack Router routes and strict search parameters; - one cached, deeply frozen YAML hydration result; - Lexical editors for authored prose; - React Flow graph rendering and interaction; - shadcn preset `b0` components normalized to the project's Base UI and styling rules; - Immer-backed local state; and - view-only route, selection, position, dialog, and draft state. ## Technology - TypeScript 6, React 19, and Vite 8 - TanStack Router in a client-side Vite application - pnpm workspace - shadcn preset `b0` with Base UI - Lexical for authored text - React Flow for graph rendering and interaction - Immer for local state transitions - Zod and `fp-ts` `Either` results at validation boundaries - SHA-256 over canonical JSON for integrity digests - YAML for the local fixture - Vitest, Testing Library, ESLint, and TypeScript project references Diamond synchronized the project documentation for [Lexical](https://lexical.dev/docs/intro) and [React Flow](https://reactflow.dev/api-reference). ## Run it Vite 8 requires Node.js `^20.19.0` or `>=22.12.0`. Use pnpm to install and run the workspace. A tracked project-wide tool-version pin remains to be added. ```bash pnpm install pnpm dev ``` Regenerate the checked-in fixture through the public application path: ```bash pnpm state:generate ``` Run the verification gates: ```bash pnpm test:run pnpm typecheck pnpm lint pnpm build ``` After bundled assets and the local fixture load, application code initiates no external API, data, or model requests. This is a source-level property of v0.2.0, not a real-browser network conformance result. ## Verification and provenance On 23 August 2026, this release-readiness pass ran against the working tree based on commit `8dc42d5`. An isolated Vitest run collected 28 test files and observed all 201 named tests pass with no skips or todos. Typecheck, lint, and the Vite build also passed. An earlier concurrent gate run exhausted two 10-second fixture hooks; the complete isolated rerun passed. Deterministic fixture regeneration had passed the preceding implementation acceptance. This review did not rewrite the protected fixture. The build reports a non-blocking main-chunk size advisory. The public documentation set is: - [Architecture](ARCHITECTURE.md) records the implemented v0.2.0 contract. - [AEGIS](aegis.md) records the working specification abstract and paper plan. - [Semantic map](SEMANTIC-MAP.md) records vocabulary ownership. - [Implications](implications.readme.md) records the initial byline and the subsequent standards, implementation, and applications adjudication. - [`prototype.state.yaml`](prototype.state.yaml) is the complete public corpus, including captured Source text, exact Evidence spans, Origins, and graph authority. - [V0.1.0 retrospective](retro.readme.md) records the first implementation, its mistakes, and unresolved product questions. - [Licensing](LICENSING.md), [third-party notices](THIRD_PARTY_NOTICES.md), and [contribution terms](CONTRIBUTING.md) define the public rights and review boundary. The local workspace also retains detailed research and adversarial review artifacts under `.private/`. That directory is deliberately excluded from the public repository, so these public documents do not rely on links into it. Maintainer commits use Git SSH signatures. A clone can opt into repository-local identity verification with the committed allowlist: ```bash git config gpg.format ssh git config gpg.ssh.allowedSignersFile .allowed_signers git log --show-signature ``` An allowlisted signature verifies the key and commit bytes. It does not prove the historical claims in the fixture or replace review of the change. ## Iterations and learnings ### v0.1.0: the interaction worked, the model did not V0.1.0 proved that a local workbench could turn an Utterance into a visible, sourced argument graph using Lexical, React Flow, Immer, and YAML. Its 70 tests and production build passed. The model mixed concerns that needed different owners. RelDef carried roles, endpoint constraints, presentation, and application prose. IDs doubled as human-readable keys. `PropositionSchema` and persisted `PropertyValue` records competed with ontology Claim. Evidence could arrive after a Claim. Origin lineage stood in for correction history. Thesis meaning leaked into ontology, UI switches, and fixture shape. Package separation existed on disk but not in the contracts. That version proved feasibility and identified the wrong abstractions. It did not justify release, and no deployment occurred. ### v0.2.0: structure, provenance, and meaning have separate owners V0.2.0 keeps the useful interaction and replaces the model beneath it. Definition families own stable keys. Exact Definitions own executable structure. Ontology Claim is the sole property assertion. Evidence attachment is first-party and atomic. System supersession makes correction explicit. Topology holds consumer-owned graph meaning. Commands and projections keep that meaning out of ontology and UI code. The fuller corpus mattered. Five hand-picked Claims could not expose where a closed relation vocabulary was honest, where it was missing a word, or where support for one reading could be misrepresented as support for another. ## Roadmap ### v0.1.0 - [x] Build the router-only Vite workbench. - [x] Integrate Lexical, React Flow, shadcn, Immer, and YAML. - [x] Exercise an Utterance-to-argument workflow. - [x] Capture a real NARA Source and exact Evidence span. - [x] Record the retrospective and withhold deployment. ### v0.2.0 - [x] Separate stable Definition families from exact revisions. - [x] Narrow RelDef to neutral binary structure. - [x] Implement grounded Claims and first-party evidence attachment. - [x] Implement pure AppendPlans, process-authenticated candidates, and atomic in-memory settlement. - [x] Implement system supersession and current-head projection. - [x] Implement `theseus.topology/v1` with deterministic limits. - [x] Establish thesis Definitions and Topology through ontology. - [x] Migrate the YAML fixture by meaning. - [x] Expand the original Utterance to four readings and 26 researched assertions. - [x] Project thesis meaning into the four-view React Flow and Lexical UI. - [x] Exercise a second consumer boundary without ontology changes. - [x] Complete tranche-level red teams and final UI acceptance. ### Later proofs - [ ] Test remote REST and MCP adapters against the same conformance corpus. - [ ] Add authenticated actor signatures and external root anchoring. - [ ] Add non-text Evidence selectors. - [ ] Add multi-user coordination and persistent storage. - [ ] Add browser-level keyboard, viewport, and visual regression tests. - [ ] Exercise larger graphs and versioned quota policies. - [ ] Decide whether and how to ship after human review. ## What v0.2.0 demonstrates The implementation demonstrates that a reusable ontology can be opinionated about identity, structure, provenance, and lifecycle without owning thesis meaning. The source, checked fixture, and local tests also demonstrate that: - a consumer can establish a local semantic contract through public ontology behavior; - every committed Claim can retain inspectable Source and Evidence provenance; - append-only correction does not require truth-by-timestamp; - one closed Topology language can qualify application-specific arrangements; - the same guarded command types can serve future human and agent clients, although v0.2.0 authenticates neither principal; - a UI can render application meaning without becoming another ontology; and - a second consumer contract can reach candidate evaluation without adding branches to ontology. The result is inspectable. A reviewer can move from an argument edge to the consumer rule that gave it meaning, then to the ontology Claim, exact Evidence span, immutable local Source capture, Origin, and history head. The storyboard boundary test can construct a different candidate interpretation over the same ontology mechanics. ## Possible improvements V0.2.0 is a serious local prototype, not a universal graph system. These improvements are ordered by dependency. They are not a release commitment. 1. **Make the public baseline reproducible.** Add tracked Node and pnpm pins, clean-checkout verification, CI, and public evidence for claims that should survive outside the local workspace. 2. **Define the trust and threat model.** Name the protected assets, adversaries, trust boundaries, principal types, key lifecycle, and exact authority required for each operation. Process-local object branding is not principal authentication. 3. **Design durable state and concurrency.** Add an append-preserving store, compare-and-swap or transactional settlement, durable idempotency receipts, multi-writer conflict rules, crash recovery, backup, and restore tests. 4. **Anchor history outside its persistence owner.** Sign checkpoints and bind them to an independently controlled log, timestamp, or witness before claiming protection from whole-history replacement. 5. **Establish Source custody.** Record retrieval method, response metadata, capture time, content hash, transformations, archival reference, license, and retention. Keep asserted locators distinct from verified retrieval. 6. **Define migration and compatibility.** Version stored aggregates, Definitions, graph bindings, Topologies, commands, projections, quotas, and canonicalization rules. Prove restore, upgrade, and rollback across released versions. 7. **Add authenticated and authorized services.** Bind credentials to principals and authorize commands by action, resource, workspace, and purpose. Preserve denial results and durable state exactly. 8. **Add agent draft and review policy.** Keep proposed command sets outside accepted ontology state until the consumer's approval policy succeeds. Record model and tool provenance without treating it as correctness proof. 9. **Support rich Evidence.** Add page and region selectors, quote selectors, table cells and formula lineage, image regions, audio and video intervals, OCR, datasets, and transformed captures while retaining exact Source-version binding. Exercise Attribution in the public corpus. 10. **Build a Topology workbench.** Add schema-aware authoring, static diagnostics, per-rule explanation, simulation, diff, approval, staged activation, rollback, and migration. Extend thesis rules to completed Argument containment and path completeness, and decide how to represent the five known missing neutral relation words. Add end-to-end cases proving that historical exact Definition selectors remain pinned after later Definition and graph-binding activation. 11. **Expose correction and head management.** Let users inspect history, compare current heads, correct Claims and Rels, retain or resolve branches, and preview every forced `supersedes` consequence. 12. **Complete a second consumer.** Give storyboard or another domain its own package, manifest, Definitions, Topology, commands, projection, fixture, and UI or CLI. Run the same conformance corpus across both consumers. 13. **Specify transport conformance.** Define one transport-neutral command, result, and error contract, then implement REST and MCP adapters.
